name: GMMPS spectral density rho(M) (4.5) and its Stieltjes transform J (4.17)

source.located: arXiv:2604.01047v1 [math-ph], 1 Apr 2026: Galanda, Meda, Murro, Pinamonti, Schmid, 'The Semiclassical Einstein-Klein-Gordon System: Asymptotic Analysis of Minkowski Spacetime'. published_statement: (4.5) p.41: K_0[phi] = Box INT_{4m^2}^inf rho(M) G^M_ret(phi) dM, rho(M) = (1/(16 pi^2)) sqrt(1 - 4m^2/M) (1/M). (3.12)-(3.13) p.27-28: K_0 = Box INT varrho(M)/M G_ret(x,M) dM with 'the positive-defined spectral density' varrho(M) = (1/(16 pi^2)) sqrt(1-4m^2/M) Theta(M-4m^2), so rho = varrho/M. (4.17) p.48 (Prop 4.10): 'the Stieltjes transform of the density rho(M) given in (4.5), described by the complex-valued function J(z) := INT_{4m^2}^inf rho(M)/(M - z) dM = (1/(8 pi^2)) ( 1/z - (4m^2 - z) m arccsc(2m/sqrt z) / (m sqrt(4m^2 - z) z^{3/2}) ), z in D', with (4.18) D = {z in C | Im z != 0 or (Im z = 0, Re z < 4m^2)}. J(0) is not stated in the source. Positivity of rho is used verbatim in Lemma 4.13's proof ('rho(M) is positive and thus the integration function is positive'); monotonicity of J is not stated as such (Prop 4.5 states monotonicity of F(w^2) = (w^2+c) g(-w^2) for general positive varsigma).
published_hypotheses: H1 free real Klein-Gordon scalar of mass m > 0 with curvature coupling xi, on Minkowski (R^4, eta)
H2 Poincare-vacuum (Hadamard) two-point function G_+ = omega_0,2; rho is the Kallen-Lehmann density of G_+^2 (pp.28-29), i.e. a one-loop, free-field quantity
H3 rho supported on M >= 4m^2 (two-particle threshold), Theta(M - 4m^2)
H4 J defined on D (4.18): the complex plane cut along [4m^2, inf); the closed form (4.17) is asserted on all of D
H5 (for Lemma 4.13's use of J, not for J itself) a_1, a_2 in (-inf, 4m^2) strictly (Prop 4.12)

lacked_data: No empirical datum enters (4.5) or (4.17): rho is the Kallen-Lehmann density of the square of the free massive vacuum two-point function, a closed-form one-loop computation in m, and J is its Stieltjes transform. There is therefore nothing the authors could have lacked in the measurement sense; the conclusion is exact for every m > 0. Evidence either way: (for) exact agreement of the printed closed form with the defining integral on the whole cut plane D to ~1e-34..1e-40, agreement of GMMPS's two separately printed forms (4.17) and Prop 4.5's L(K), and exact agreement of the normalisation with the independent 2002 AMM computation (B37a,b); (against) none found. What the result genuinely cannot carry is model content, not data: it is the free-field, vacuum-state, one-loop density (H1, H2) with m > 0; an interacting or strongly coupled field (e.g. 2512.00503's holographic matter) or the massless limit (J(0) ~ 1/m^2 diverges) falls outside it. Those are named hypotheses, not missing data, and the tree uses J only inside GMMPS's own free-scalar setting.

Re-derivation (sympy + mpmath + z3, 22/22 PASS): J(0) = 1/(96 pi^2 m^2) exact from the integral and from both one-sided limits of (4.17); (4.17) = defining integral on all of D (real axis both sides of 0, complex z in all quadrants, Re z > 4m^2 off-axis) to <= 3.5e-34 relative; Im(4.17) = 0 on real z < 4m^2; rho >= 0 on M >= 4m^2; J strictly increasing on real z < 4m^2; the tree's bracket bound 4J(0)/(4+|g|) <= J(g) <= J(0) machine-checked for g <= 0 (z3 unsat) and its failure for g > 0 shown as a control; normalisation independently confirmed against AMM (B37). No datum enters. Discrepancies recorded, none repaired and none affecting the result: (i) the printed (4.17) carries a redundant m/m factor; (ii) p.41 writes check-varrho + b_2 h_2 where p.48-50 write check-rho + b_2 h_2 (notation, since rho = varrho/M, not a different object); (iii) the tree's bracket-bound docstrings leave the guard g <= 0 implicit (M/(M+|g|)); every call site satisfies it.
